scripts/lib/ceo-asks.sh.evidence: ca_resolve reads the finite CA_REPOS_KEY declaration; remaining routines read separate TODO records.
scripts/lib/ceo-asks.sh.presence: ca_resolve checks for the declaration file

scripts/lib/ceo-ruled.sh.evidence: cr_resolve reads CR_PATHS_KEY then follows ca_resolve when the explicit ruling path is absent.
scripts/lib/ceo-ruled.sh.presence: cr_resolve checks for the declaration file

scripts/lib/mutation-harness.sh#copy.evidence: mutation_copy_engine copies configuration bytes without reading their meaning; the invoking suite supplies the downstream executed readers.

scripts/hooks/contract-integrity-probe.s.evidence: Q copies the governed config into Q_ENT before q_env executes the workspace guards. The enclosing Q consumer must follow those executed guards.

scripts/lib/resolve-main-checkout.sh.evidence: Resolves Git common-directory paths; does not read configuration values.

scripts/lib/resolve-roots.sh#roots.evidence: Root resolution and adoption test marker presence. Namespace/agent lookup functions below this region are not invoked by these guards.
scripts/lib/resolve-roots.sh#roots.presence: Root candidates test orchestration.config existence, never its values.

scripts/lib/seat-jurisdiction.sh.evidence: Physical path and Git jurisdiction helpers test adoption-marker existence. They do not source configuration or read its keys.
scripts/lib/seat-jurisdiction.sh.presence: richos_governing_root tests the candidate repository adoption marker.

scripts/lib/unevaluated-notice.sh.evidence: Parses payload JSON and writes a deduplicated diagnostic under the supplied entity root; no orchestration-config read.

scripts/hooks/guard-main-checkout-writes.evidence: Sources the governed configuration and reads PROTECTED_PATHS for empty/adopted checks and path matching, including the governing-root reload.

scripts/hooks/guard-bash-main-writes.sh.evidence: Sources the governed configuration and passes only PROTECTED_PATHS to the embedded classifier as GUARD_TREES.

scripts/hooks/guard-main-checkout-writes.evidence: The real engine config supplies protected paths to generated payloads. Every hook call explicitly governs that engine root; no other config value is asserted.

scripts/hooks/guard-bash-main-writes.tes.evidence: The real config supplies only PROTECTED_PATHS. The suite writes that one value into its private config; the empty-value arm supplies a separate constant config.

scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-ban.sh.evidence: The production path sources the governed config and reads BAN_WORKFLOW_TOOL. Embedded self-tests use separately generated configs.

scripts/lib/ci_pause.py.evidence: Reads the separately located CI pause JSON and optionally Git remote URLs. It does not open or source orchestration.config.

scripts/hooks/session-start-ci-surface.s.evidence: Reads CI_SURFACE_STATE_DIR JSON, a HOME-relative launch agent and the separate CI pause registry. It does not load orchestration.config.

scripts/hooks/notice-waiver-repetition.p.evidence: Source discovery scans script .sh/.py text and record discovery scans state logs. These functions neither execute discovered scripts nor read orchestration.config.

scripts/check-census.py.evidence: Reads registration/dispatcher inventories and hook source text as data, importing only the waiver discovery functions. It does not execute those registrations or source orchestration.config.

scripts/check-census.test.sh.evidence: C2 invokes the real Workflow guard on an engine-root payload, so BAN_WORKFLOW_TOOL is a transitive dependency despite the config basename being absent. C3 supplies private HOME and CI state to the CI notice.

scripts/lib/ceo-todos.py#items.evidence: Items mode reads the supplied JSON job then returns after parsing/rendering its embedded record. The filesystem and done-check branches below this region are not entered.

scripts/lib/ceo-asks.py.evidence: Reads only the supplied job JSON and applies matching predicates; no configuration lookup.

scripts/lib/stop-hook-notice.sh.evidence: Parses supplied payload and reads/writes the supplied entity-root notice state; no orchestration configuration lookup.

scripts/hooks/notice-ceo-asks.sh.evidence: Resolves the governed root then delegates config access to ca_resolve. Its other inputs are the hook payload and per-session ledger.

scripts/hooks/guard-ceo-ask-first.sh.evidence: Resolves the governed root then delegates config access to ca_resolve. Its other inputs are the hook payload and per-session ledger.

scripts/hooks/notice-ceo-unasked.sh.evidence: Resolves the governed root then delegates config access to ca_resolve. Its other inputs are the hook payload and per-session ledger.

scripts/hooks/session-start-ceo-ask.sh.evidence: Resolves the governed root then delegates config access to ca_resolve. Its other inputs are the hook payload and per-session ledger.

scripts/ceo-asks-status.sh.evidence: Uses the supplied entity-root argument, delegates config access to ca_resolve and reads that root’s ask ledger.

scripts/lib/stopwatch.sh.evidence: Obtains clock values from shell builtins, date, Perl or Python. No configuration lookup.

scripts/lib/cpu_policy.py.evidence: Pure CPU percentage and admission predicates; no configuration or file reads.

scripts/lib/operator_fences.py#proc.evidence: Kernel process-generation routines read libproc or /proc only. Fence/lease commands below this region are not invoked by the process supervisor.

scripts/lib/cpu_guard.py.evidence: Token and supervisor callers use registration, health, admission and verification-client APIs before HostMemory. These read native process data and their private controller records, never orchestration.config. They do not invoke the watch/install CLI or its HostMemory provider. Caller commands remain separate declared edges.

scripts/lib/proc_tree.py.evidence: Supervises the caller’s command and samples owned processes. Its own inputs are environment, process identity and controller state, never orchestration settings.

scripts/lib/engine_pass.py.evidence: Admission/slot policy reads its own records, Git identity and process generations; no orchestration settings.

scripts/lib/worker_tokens.py.evidence: Worker leases read their budget files and invoke the caller’s separately declared command, through process supervision and admission policy.

scripts/lib/mutation-pool.sh.evidence: Runs the supplied mutation callback with worker leases; its own configuration is operational environment. Actual callback/helper relationships belong to each harness.

scripts/hooks/ceo-asks.test.sh.evidence: Creates a private entity config and private TODO declaration from literal values. Every hook/status invocation receives that entity root. Real hooks.json, installer, probe and notice text are read as registration/source data only. It never transports the real config. Nested mutations rebuild the same fixtures.

scripts/hooks/ceo-asks.mutation.sh.evidence: Copies a finite hook/helper list, never the real configuration. Thirteen literal mutations change matching, gating and reporting, not config provenance. Nested ceo-asks.test.sh reconstructs private configs before execution.

scripts/lib/ceo-todos.sh#ask-items.evidence: Reads the separate .ceo-todos declaration, supplied record, markdown entry points and cold-open records. Config keys here are CT_* declaration fields, not orchestration settings. This contract is used only by ca_items_json, which calls ct_load_declaration, ct_resolve_roots and ct_items.

scripts/lib/verification_inputs.py#confi.evidence: The config parser accepts assignment text as data, preserving key references and rejecting unsupported executable syntax. No selected hook or suite is invoked.

scripts/lib/affected_units.py#validate-c.evidence: validate_config reads the real config and its declared key registry, rejecting unsupported syntax and unknown keys.
scripts/lib/affected_units.py#validate-c.whole: global assignment syntax and key-registry validation

scripts/verification-config.test.sh.evidence: Runs only --validate-config; this is the whole-config validation obligation.
